catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from the cas_runner repository, focusing on orchestration, governance, skills, LLM abstraction, and agent configuration. Evidence is based on file paths and symbol names; full source bodies were not available for every entry.
analysis_limits: Code bodies not fully inspected; symbols and paths only
Agent runtime behaviour inferred from configuration files, not execution logs
FlowRunner step contract not directly visible in provided key files

system_map.overview: This is a governance-centric agent toolchain where an LLM-driven FlowRunner executes sequence-based workflows, a compliance engine gates agent outputs, and declarative skills/verifier subagents shape agent behaviour. Persistent architecture knowledge is stored in cas-knowledge and treated as a blackboard for agents.

agents.name: CAS Agent
agents.role: Executes architecture workflows using declared skills and follows governance rules in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md

agents.name: Verifier Agent
agents.role: Independently checks candidate outputs before acceptance, reducing self-confirmation bias

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: System-level orchestrator that runs a sequence of steps with a shared context

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates agent-generated artifacts against governance rules and emits structured findings

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Decides whether governance actions are allowed based on a transition registry

orchestration.description: FlowRunner provides centralised sequential orchestration for pipeline execution, while skills and verifier subagents give agents local autonomy within governance boundaries. Compliance and action engines act as centralised gates.

patterns.name: Pluggable LLM Provider with Mock Fallback

tool_protocols.notes: LLM access is wrapped by client classes; no MCP or direct tool-calling protocol observed.

optimisation_targets.notes: Abstraction allows swapping provider and deterministic mock runs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: A minimal client interface focuses on execution stability rather than advanced agent autonomy.

patterns.summary: LLM calls are isolated behind a client abstraction with a mock implementation, enabling deterministic execution and provider portability.
patterns.intent: Decouple the orchestration logic from a specific LLM vendor and support deterministic tests.
patterns.context: Both a production LiteLLM client and a mock client are present in the LLM layer, suggesting the runner can execute with or without a live provider.
forces: Provider APIs differ in request/response shapes
Tests need deterministic outputs
Production calls must remain flexible
patterns.solution: Define a small client interface used by the FlowRunner, provide a LiteLLM-based implementation and a mock implementation that returns canned responses.
implementation_signals: Two client classes with the same expected interface

evidence.note: Production LLM adapter using LiteLLM.
Deterministic fake client for tests and offline execution.

failure_modes: Mock behaviour drifts from real provider semantics
Provider-specific features become inaccessible

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse any time an agent pipeline needs to be testable without a live LLM; keep the interface narrow to avoid leaking provider-specific types.

patterns.name: Shared-Context Sequential Pipeline

tool_protocols.notes: Pipeline steps appear to share a mutable context; no protocol-level tool calling evident.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential execution gives predictable state at the cost of parallel speed.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Each step executes in a fixed order with a shared context, keeping control central and explicit.

patterns.summary: The runner executes a sequence of steps, passing a single mutable context through the pipeline so each step sees prior results.
patterns.intent: Provide a predictable, linear execution model for multi-step agent workflows without introducing task-level scheduling complexity.
patterns.context: FlowRunner is the central execution class; cli.py and bootstrap.py likely initialize it with a flow definition.
forces: Steps often depend on outputs from earlier steps
A single agent or orchestrator must own the flow
Debugging is easier with a linear execution trace
patterns.solution: FlowRunner iterates over registered steps; each step reads and mutates a shared context object, optionally writing artifacts, and the next step uses those artifacts as inputs.
implementation_signals: FlowRunner class with an execute method
Context object passed as an argument to each step

evidence.note: Likely runs a step list with a shared context.

costs: Steps become coupled to context keys
failure_modes: Step order change breaks downstream assumptions
Undocumented context keys become implicit contracts

patterns.reuse_notes: Use this when workflows are inherently sequential and you want a single deterministic execution trace. Keep context schemas typed and documented.

patterns.name: Post-hoc Compliance Gate

tool_protocols.notes: Evaluation is performed by a dedicated engine after generation rather than during generation.

optimisation_targets.notes: The gate focuses on preventing non-compliant proposals from proceeding.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can generate freely, but a separate system-level check curtails autonomy at the boundary.

patterns.summary: Agent-generated outputs are validated against governance rules by a separate compliance engine that returns structured findings.
patterns.intent: Prevent non-compliant architecture proposals from reaching promotion or production.
patterns.context: Used after generator steps and before approval/promotion; emits ComplianceFinding objects and aggregate ComplianceMetrics.
forces: LLM outputs are non-deterministic and may violate rules
Rules need to be auditable and traceable
The gate must be cheap enough to run regularly
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine inspects the generated artifact against a rule set, produces structured findings, and reports metrics such as failure counts and risk levels.
implementation_signals: ComplianceEngine class with an evaluation method

evidence.note: Evaluates artifacts and returns compliance findings.
Typed structures for compliance results.

costs: Extra evaluation step in the pipeline
failure_modes: Rules become stale
Gate is by-passed in some code paths
Metric aggregation hides important details

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse whenever LLM-generated output must be constrained by an external policy. Keep the rule engine separate from the generator to avoid self-validation.

patterns.name: Controlled State-Transition Registry

tool_protocols.notes: Action eligibility is determined by a transition table, not by LLM discretion.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents arbitrary governance state changes without proper sequencing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomy is limited by explicitly encoded state transitions.

patterns.summary: Governance actions are permitted only when a transition registry says the current state and requested action are compatible.
patterns.intent: Make governance state changes auditable and prevent invalid lifecycle jumps.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine and TransitionRegistry exist alongside GovernanceActionService, suggesting an action-eligibility layer between requests and mutation.
forces: Agent-driven governance changes must be reversible or staged
Unconstrained transitions could corrupt architecture state
Transitions should be readable by humans and machines
patterns.solution: Define a mapping (registry) of allowed transitions; before performing a GovernanceAction, the engine checks the registry and rejects out-of-sequence actions.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class that stores allowed source/destination pairs
GovernanceActionEngine calls registry before applying action

evidence.note: Likely encodes allowed state transitions and guards actions.
Represents the action being requested.

failure_modes: Registry becomes incomplete and blocks legitimate actions
Transitions are duplicated in different code paths
Action semantics change without registry update

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse when agents or services need to progress through lifecycle states in a controlled manner; centralise all transition rules in one registry.

patterns.name: Traceable Governance Metrics

tool_protocols.notes: Metrics are derived from explicit trace records rather than inferred ad-hoc state.

optimisation_targets.notes: Metrics aim to provide an accurate, auditable picture of governance health.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents influence governance, but the health signal is computed in a centralised, evidence-based manner.

patterns.summary: Governance health, throughput, and risk indicators are derived from a traceable metric model instead of subjective or ad-hoc scoring.
patterns.intent: Make the health of the architecture governance process measurable and explainable.
patterns.context: Models like TraceableMetric, GovernanceInventory, GovernanceHealth, GovernanceThroughput, and GovernanceRisks appear alongside a dashboard health model.
forces: Governance decisions need a defensible audit trail
Operators need a quick health summary
Raw events must be aggregated without losing traceability
patterns.solution: Every governance event contributes a traceable metric; aggregation layers produce inventory, health, throughput, and risk views from those metrics.

evidence.note: Typed models for traceable governance state and derived metrics.
Computes health status from aggregate governance data.

failure_modes: Traces become incomplete
Aggregation rules lose edge cases
Health metric is gamed by agents or users

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt when agent/system trust depends on verifiable metrics; store raw events in a trace log and derive statuses in a separate projection.

patterns.name: Declarative Skill Packs

tool_protocols.notes: Skills are exposed as directory conventions rather than tool-calling APIs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Skills package common workflows so agents do not re-plan from scratch.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can choose which skill to invoke but are guided by fixed instructions.

patterns.summary: Agent capabilities are packaged as declarative directories (skills) containing instructions, templates, and evaluation cases, making workflows reusable.
patterns.intent: Give agents a predictable, versioned way to perform domain workflows without re-deriving steps each time.
patterns.context: Several cas-* skill folders exist (add or modify feature, audit agent rules, drawio generator, refactor knowledge links, refactor module, sync archgov reviews, hf-cli) and are mirrored between .agents and .claude.
forces: Common agent tasks should be consistent across sessions
Skills need to be discoverable
Skills should be evolvable without changing agent core logic
patterns.solution: Each skill is a directory with markdown instructions; the agent can load a skill and follow its steps. Skill evaluation models allow asserting skill correctness.
implementation_signals: SkillEvalSuite and SkillAssertions models in skills/models.py

evidence.note: Declarative skill folders for common agent tasks.
Skills duplicated for the Claude runtime.
Models for evaluating skill behaviour.

costs: Agents may over-rely on fixed scripts
failure_modes: Skills drift from actual best practices
Mirroring fails and runtimes diverge
Skill instructions are ambiguous

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when you want to codify common agent workflows. Keep each skill self-contained and pair it with an evaluation suite to prevent drift.

patterns.name: Independent Verifier Agent

tool_protocols.notes: Verification is a separate agent role with its own instructions.

optimisation_targets.notes: The verifier reduces self-confirmation bias by providing an independent review.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: The generating agent still has freedom, but a separate agent is required to approve its output.

patterns.summary: A dedicated verifier subagent is defined for both .agents and .claude, giving the main agent an independent second opinion before acceptance.
patterns.intent: Catch errors and biases that a generating agent might miss.
patterns.context: Both agent ecosystems include a verifier subagent definition, suggesting the main agent delegates review to this secondary role.
forces: LLM output can contain subtle mistakes
Single-agent self-review is often optimistic
A second agent costs extra LLM calls
patterns.solution: Define a verifier agent with instructions to check outputs against expectations; the main agent or orchestrator should use its verdict to approve or reject.
implementation_signals: Verifier role has explicit rejection criteria

evidence.note: Defines a verifier subagent for the primary agent runtime.
Mirrors the verifier role for Claude Code.

failure_modes: Verifier prompts become too lax
Verifier is ignored by main agent
Verifier re-implements the same logic as generator

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in any flow where correctness matters and a single LLM pass is not enough. Keep the verifier prompts independent from the generator prompts.

patterns.name: Multi-Runtime Agent Config Synchronisation

tool_protocols.notes: Configuration is synchronised to multiple agent runtimes rather than shared via a protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures agents in different ecosystems operate under the same governance rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: One authoritative config block is copied/symlinked to multiple runtimes to reduce divergence.

patterns.summary: Bootstrap merges governance blocks into agent configuration files and syncs skills/agents between runtimes so all agents see one canonical rule set.
patterns.intent: Keep Claude Code, generic agents, and CAS-specific configuration aligned to prevent governance drift.
patterns.context: bootstrap.py merges CAS governance blocks into Claude settings and AGENTS.md-style files, and creates symlinks or copies for skill directories.
forces: Different agent runtimes have different config file formats
Governance rules should be single-sourced
Skill directories must exist in the right place for each runtime
patterns.solution: A bootstrap command merges the canonical governance block into each runtime's config and replicates skill/agent directories using symlinks where possible, or copies as fallback.

evidence.note: Propagates governance config and syncs skill/agent directories.

failure_modes: Overwritten local customisations
Symlink broken after repo move
Copy becomes stale if not re-run

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse when you need to keep multiple agent ecosystems aligned; prefer symlinks to avoid duplicated drift, and make bootstrap idempotent.

patterns.name: Rule-Context Injection

tool_protocols.notes: Rules are provided as executable context files rather than through dynamic tool calls.

optimisation_targets.notes: Gives the agent actionable constraints before it plans or performs actions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents operate within a prepared rule context, reducing free-form planning risk.

patterns.summary: Runtime rule context and execution profile are loaded from disk and injected into agent workflows, giving agents a fixed set of constraints to plan against.
patterns.intent: Provide an explicit, versioned set of rules and execution preferences to the agent before it acts.
patterns.context: The runtime directory contains rule-context.json and execution-profile.yaml, suggesting these are consumed by the runner or agent startup.
forces: Agent needs to reason under governance constraints
Rules should be easy to update without code changes
Execution behavior should be configurable per environment
patterns.solution: Store a structured rule context and execution profile as data files; load them during runner bootstrap and pass the data into the agent's context.

evidence.note: Likely contains governance rules to be injected into the agent context.
Likely contains execution preferences or defaults.

benefits: Clear separation of policy and code
Easier to audit which rules were active
costs: Rules can become too many to fit in context
failure_modes: Rule context is not loaded
Rule conflicts with system constraints
Context size grows and degrades response quality

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for any system where agents need structured policy input; version the rule files and log/load the exact context used for each run.

patterns.name: Persistent Knowledge Blackboard

tool_protocols.notes: Knowledge is stored as files in a shared directory tree rather than in a live protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Persistent knowledge lets agents reuse prior decisions and avoid re-derivation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents are given a rich persistent state to operate from, but must conform to its structure.

patterns.summary: Architecture knowledge is stored in a persistent, versioned directory structure (cas-knowledge) that agents read and write as a shared blackboard.
patterns.intent: Provide a persistent, human- and agent-readable source of architectural truth to inform agent decisions.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge contains global decisions, governance, maps, models, narratives, patterns, rules, signals, and per-project state, plus templates for new artifacts.
forces: Agent decisions should be grounded in accumulated knowledge
Knowledge must be versionable and auditable
Artifacts must have a consistent structure for reuse
patterns.solution: Structure the workspace as a knowledge base with directories for each artifact type; agents read relevant files before generating and write new artifacts back in the same structure.
implementation_signals: Template files for new decisions, ADRs, patterns, signals, etc.

evidence.note: Persistent store of past architecture decisions.
Governance rules used by agents and compliance engine.
Template for new ADR artifacts.

failure_modes: Knowledge files become stale
Agents ignore the existing knowledge
Structure changes break older references

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a filesystem-as-blackboard when the knowledge corpus is primarily text and must be version controlled; define strong templates to keep the corpus parseable.

patterns.name: CI Workflow Validation Gate

tool_protocols.notes: Validation is performed by static checks over workflow YAML, not by the LLM agent.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents CI workflows from introducing non-reproducible or broken automation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agent-generated CI changes are constrained by deterministic static validations.

patterns.summary: A validation script checks CI workflows for syntax, pinning, hardcoding, and retired workflow issues, acting as a deterministic guardrail on agent-modified automation.
patterns.intent: Prevent agents or humans from committing CI workflows that are brittle, non-reproducible, or obsolete.
patterns.context: A validation script is present under specs/090-simplify-cicd-workflows; it appears to be run in CI to enforce workflow quality.
forces: CI workflows are often edited by agents or copy-pasted
Unpinned installers and hardcoded values break reproducibility
Retired workflows add confusion and cost
patterns.solution: Automate a series of checks over workflow YAMLs: YAML syntax, absence of hardcoded configuration, pinned installers, no unreachable dry-run, no retired workflows, proper triggers, and adoption of composite actions.

evidence.note: Static validation rules for CI workflow quality.

failure_modes: Checks miss new workflow patterns
Checks become too strict and are bypassed
Retired workflow detection is stale

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse in any repo where CI workflows are agent-edited; implement as a standalone script and run in a PR check.

patterns.name: Skill Evaluation Suite

tool_protocols.notes: Skills are evaluated through structured test cases and assertions, not ad-hoc manual review.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables continuous regression checks on agent workflows.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Skills can evolve, but their behaviour is pinned by an evaluation suite.

patterns.summary: Skills are paired with typed evaluation cases, assertions, suites, and reports so agent workflows can be tested and monitored.
patterns.intent: Catch skill regressions and ensure skills behave as documented.
patterns.context: Skill models include EvalStatus, SkillAssertions, SkillEvalCase, SkillEvalSuite, SkillEvalResult, and SkillEvalReport; a CI workflow references skill evaluations.
forces: Skills are prompt-based and may change behaviour over time
Manual verification of skills is expensive
Skill updates need confidence they still work
patterns.solution: Define skill evaluation cases with assertions; run them in CI to produce a report that can be used as a quality gate.

evidence.note: Typed evaluation model for skills.
CI workflow for running skill evaluations.

failure_modes: Assertions are too weak to catch issues
Suite becomes stale after skill updates
CI skips evals due to time constraints

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for any prompt-based reusable workflow; store evaluation cases alongside the skill and run them in CI.

patterns.name: Health Dashboard Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Health is a derived projection over governance state, not a direct agent output.

optimisation_targets.notes: Gives operators a quick, traceable view of system health.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Health is centralised and computed from consistent inputs, limiting subjective interpretation.

patterns.summary: A health model computes status and reasons from governance metrics, producing an operator-facing projection of the agent-governance system's health.
patterns.intent: Summarise complex governance and execution state into a single health signal with explainable reasons.
patterns.context: This file sits alongside governance models and likely consumes GovernanceHealth/Risks to render a dashboard.
forces: Operators need a quick health status
Health must be explainable to be trusted
Metrics change over time
patterns.solution: Define a HealthStatus enum and a calculate_health function that takes governance metrics and returns status plus a list of reasons.

evidence.note: Computes health status and explanation from metrics.

failure_modes: Health thresholds misaligned with actual risk
Reasons list becomes stale
Dashboard not updated in real time

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when you need an aggregated health indicator from varied metrics; keep the calculation pure and expose reasons for transparency.

anti_patterns.name: Duplicated Agent Configuration Across Runtimes
symptoms: Same skills exist in .agents and .claude as separate copies
A bootstrap script is needed to sync them
If sync is not run, agents see different instructions

where_observed.note: Explicitly syncing skill directories suggests duplication is a known pain point.
Skills are duplicated from .agents rather than single-sourced.

impact: Agents in different runtimes drift apart
Governance rules are not applied uniformly
Debugging differences across runtimes becomes costly
suggested_remediation: Prefer symlinks over copies where the filesystem supports it
Make the sync script a pre-commit or CI step
Use a single source directory and generate runtime-specific entry points

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned Installer Dependency in CI
symptoms: CI workflows install tools without pinned versions
Validation script explicitly checks for unpinned installers

where_observed.note: The presence of this check indicates unpinned installers were a recurring problem.

suggested_remediation: Pin all installer versions in CI workflows
Automate renovation of pinned versions with controlled review

anti_patterns.name: Retired Workflow Accumulation
symptoms: Old workflows remain in the repository after being replaced
Runner picks up unused branches or triggers
Validation script has a check for retired workflow definitions

where_observed.note: Explicitly checks for retired workflow leftovers.

impact: Confusion about which workflow is authoritative
Unused automation still consumes CI minutes
Security surface expands with old triggers

Keep a migration note in a changelog
Add a stale-workflow detector to CI

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Compliance engine and transition registry act as deterministic gates around agent-generated outputs and governance state changes.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Safety is enforced centrally rather than left to agent discretion.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Traceable metrics, OpenTelemetry hooks, and health projections ensure agent execution and governance decisions are auditable.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Observability is designed in from the start, supporting trust and debug.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Skills, rule-context files, and bootstrap sync establish structured contracts for prompt/context content across agent runtimes.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Configuration is versioned and propagated centrally, reducing drift.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Mock LLM client and skill eval suites reduce the cost of running full LLM-backed workflows during testing.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Deterministic mocks allow many runs without LLM spend.
